screen.scoring.main_intro: An IS is assessed as a composition of digital assets. Each asset is rated on the RES pillars, then the IS score is consolidated according to each asset's criticality.
screen.scoring.main_title: IRN maturity of an information system
screen.scoring.step1.intro: Each asset’s maturity is assessed using the IRN scale:
screen.scoring.step1.nc: N.C. means “Not applicable”: the criterion is explicitly answered and counts toward completion, but is excluded from the score.
screen.scoring.step1.title: 1 · Asset rating
screen.scoring.step2.p1: For each asset, OpenIRN first calculates a score per RES pillar from the rated criteria in that pillar.
screen.scoring.step2.p2: The asset pre-score E is then the geometric mean of the completed pillar scores:
screen.scoring.step2.p3: The geometric mean naturally penalizes weak links: a very low pillar pulls the asset score down more than an arithmetic mean would.
screen.scoring.step2.title: 2 · Pre-score E for each asset
screen.scoring.step3.p1: Each asset has a criticality D on 4 levels. This criticality is the asset’s weight in the overall resilience of the IS.
screen.scoring.step3.title: 3 · Asset criticality D
screen.scoring.step4.p1: The IS maturity score is the weighted geometric mean of asset pre-scores E, using D as the weight:
screen.scoring.step4.p2: A poorly rated critical asset therefore weighs much more heavily on the IS score than a low-criticality asset. The formula reflects a resilience-chain logic: the weak link must count.
screen.scoring.step4.title: 4 · IS maturity score
screen.scoring.step5.p1: In a campaign created from an IS, the “IRN score” card displays the consolidated maturity of the IS. Asset buttons let you fill in the IRN grid separately for each asset.
screen.scoring.step5.p2: Unanswered criteria do not yet participate in the score. Completion is therefore essential to interpret the rating correctly.
screen.scoring.step5.title: 5 · Reading in OpenIRN
screen.scoring.title: IRN score calculation method
